The notes app is in `notes/` (`index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js`). I only syntax-checked `app.js` with `node --check`. I haven't opened it in a browser, so the UI is untested.

What it does:
- **Notes:** You can create, edit and delete notes. Each has a title, a body and tags, and they save automatically (debounced, and flushed when you close the tab). They are kept in the browser's `localStorage`.
- **Pin and sort:** A star pins a note to the top; the rest sort by last edited.
- **Search and tags:** Search covers title, body and tags, with multiple words ANDed together. Clicking a tag chip in the sidebar filters by that tag.
- **Markdown preview:** Preview renders headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, code blocks, quotes, lists, links and horizontal rules. Task checkboxes (`- [ ]`) can be ticked in the preview and update the note's text.
- **Trash:** Deleting moves a note to Trash. Trash is emptied after 30 days, can be emptied by hand (double-click the Trash tab), and you can restore a note from it.
- **Backup:**
  - Export and import use JSON; import merges notes by id and keeps the newer copy.
  - A single note can also be downloaded as a `.md` file.
- **Dark mode:** It follows your system theme, with a manual toggle.
- **Layout and tabs:**
  - On a phone-width screen it shows one panel at a time with a back button.
  - A change made in another tab is picked up automatically.
- **Shortcuts:**
  - `Ctrl/⌘ N` creates a note.
  - `Ctrl/⌘ K` focuses search.
  - `Ctrl/⌘ E` toggles preview.
  - `Esc` clears the search box.
  - `Tab` inserts two spaces.
- **Housekeeping:**
  - A note left completely empty is discarded.
  - A Welcome note appears on first run.
  - If the browser can't save (storage full or blocked), the footer says so in red.

Notes live only in this browser, so use Export now and then to keep a backup. I left out nested-list rendering beyond simple indent, tables, images and sync between devices; say if you want any of them.
